site.name: Blue Jay Mine
overview: Blue Jay Mine is a historic fluorspar mine southeast of Jamestown in Boulder County, where federal mining studies documented a substantial underground operation and Boulder County later preserved the site as a designated historic property.

timeline.text: Federal investigators described the Blue Jay Mine as developed by several short adits, a roughly 300-foot vertical shaft, and drifts on the 150- and 300-foot levels.
Federal teams sampled and examined the mine's lower workings during investigations of uranium-bearing minerals associated with the fluorite vein.
Boulder County designated Blue Jay Mine as a historic site, recognizing the surviving mining complex near Jamestown.

moreHistory: The Blue Jay vein was described by U.S. Geological Survey investigators as a northwest-trending structure more than 1,000 feet long, containing deep-purple crystalline fluorite with quartz, clay minerals, pyrite, galena, and uranium-bearing minerals.

Boulder County has described Blue Jay as one of the better-preserved and historically interesting mining complexes on its open-space properties. The surviving hoist-house area has also become important bat habitat, giving the historic mine an additional modern conservation role.
